sections.html:
Provo is the Utah County seat, about 43 miles south of Salt Lake City on the eastern shore of Utah Lake. It spans 44.19 square miles, of which 41.69 are land and 2.50 are water, at roughly 4,550 feet, with Orem to the north and Springville to the south. ZIP codes run 84601 through 84606.

Interstate 15 crosses the west side, US 89 (State Street) runs northwest to southeast, and US 189 ties State Street, I-15, BYU and Orem together. The whitewashed Y on the mountain is the city's best-known landmark. For a seller, location relative to those roads, the campus and a transit stop is usually the first thing a buyer or tenant asks about, so put it near the top of any description.

Only 39.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, a low share that reflects the huge student population around BYU. The median age was 23.8 at the 2020 census. The city counted 115,162 residents then, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 114,527.

Since so many houses are rentals, a Provo seller often has a tenant, a lease or a school-year calendar to plan around. BYU enrolls over 30,000 students, and academic calendars affect when rentals turn over and when houses sell.

sections.h2: An old city with mixed housing
sections.html:
Fort Utah, founded in 1849 by 33 Mormon families, was the start of Provo. The city incorporated in April 1850 and was renamed for the trapper Etienne Provost. Brigham Young Academy, the forerunner of BYU, was founded in 1875, and orchards once earned Provo the name Garden City.

Housing here spans many decades, so condition varies a lot from street to street. The age of the roof, furnace and cooling equipment often comes up in a buyer's inspection. Annual precipitation is about 17.2 inches near BYU.

Provo is the southern end of the FrontRunner commuter rail line, running since December 10, 2012. The Provo Intermodal Center brings together rail, local UTA buses and Greyhound, and Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at the station daily. UVX bus rapid transit, run jointly with Orem, runs toward Utah Valley University. Provo Municipal Airport is Utah's second-busiest by aircraft movements. Mean commute time is 18.4 minutes.

Provo allows one accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a one-family detached home, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. The rules are in section 14.30.030 of the city code and carry real weight for anyone selling a house with a basement or garage apartment.

  • A rental dwelling license under Chapter 6.26 is required and renewed every year.
  • The license expires one year after approval or when the property is transferred, whichever comes first.
  • A deed restriction describing how the unit is built and occupied is recorded with the Utah County Recorder.
  • The owner must show the home is the primary residence with at least two documents, such as a driver license, vehicle registration, voter card or latest tax return.
  • No more than three adults, related or not, plus their minor children, may live in the unit.

Because the license ends on transfer, a buyer must apply again. Utah courts have upheld owner-occupancy requirements for renting an accessory unit, in Anderson v. Provo City (2005 UT 5), a case about accessory apartments in single-family zones near BYU. Cities may require a business license for short-term rentals but cannot ban a listing on an online platform.

Before state law S.B. 284, Provo allowed detached accessory dwellings only in specific overlay zones. The new statute reaches parcels of 11,000 square feet or larger with a single-family home. A policy proposal would cap accessory structures at 40 percent of the parcel, and the city has published a map of projected new eligibility. If a detached unit is part of your plans or your buyer's, check the current rule with Provo City first. Rules in this area are changing, and a promise made to a buyer today could be wrong next year, so get the answer in writing from the city if a detached unit affects the price.

Provo has its own Provo School District, with 13 elementary schools, two middle schools and three high schools. Alpine School District covers a small section of the city. Provo is outside the three new districts that replace Alpine in 2027, so its boundaries stay as they are. Parents will still ask which school an address feeds, so confirm it with the district.

Utah County does the assessing and billing, and its Auditor works in Provo itself at 100 East Center Street, Suite 3600. Expect a valuation notice at the end of July. If you dispute the market value, the Board of Equalization takes appeals until September 15, online, by email, by mail or in person. Tax notices arrive mid to late October.

Thanks to the 45% exemption, a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value if someone lives in it at least 183 consecutive days a year. A full-time tenant counts. A vacant or part-time rental is secondary and pays on full value, a rule that touches many Provo owners. The Treasurer, at 801-851-8255, gives payoff amounts on delinquent tax.

sections.h2: Selling a Provo house for cash
sections.html:
People call us about a house with tenants, a rental whose license lapsed, an inherited property or a place that needs repairs.

  1. Describe the house and any lease in place.
  2. We go through it and name a price that reflects condition.
  3. Agree, and an escrow or title company schedules closing.
  4. The county files the deed and you are paid.

We buy as-is, so there are no repairs or cleaning. Timing around leases and the school year is something we can plan with you.

Gather the deed, the newest tax notice, any lease and rent roll, and for a house with an accessory unit, the rental dwelling license and recorded deed restriction. The title company will say what else it wants. Even a short list of what you hold speeds up the first call, and most gaps can be closed as the sale proceeds. If a tenant plans to leave at the end of a school term, tell us that date so closing can be set around it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Provo house that has an accessory apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. The city wants an owner-occupied home and a rental dwelling license, and since the license ends at transfer, the buyer applies for a new one. We purchase the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Does the Provo rental license carry over to a new owner?
faqs.a: No. Per city code, it expires a year after approval or when the property transfers, whichever is first. The new owner applies.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal Provo property taxes?
faqs.a: Appeal to the Utah County Board of Equalization by September 15. Later filings, through March 31, need to meet extra criteria.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Provo deed?
faqs.a: That is the Utah County Recorder, 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo. Staff there don't draft papers, advise on law or search titles.

faqs.q: Why is Provo's owner-occupancy rate so low?
faqs.a: At 39.4% for 2020 to 2024 it reflects a big student population around BYU, with a median age of 23.8, which makes many houses rentals.
